items.title: Jackie Williams interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: I had the great pleasure of working with one of the great ladies actually, Miss Maxine Sullivan, and in fact I did a few recordings with Maxine.

ctx.x: Who are some of the vocalists that you’ve had a chance to work behind?

Oh, I had the great pleasure of working with one of the great ladies actually, Miss Maxine Sullivan, and in fact I did a few recordings with Maxine. And I think one of the last things they did was a Burton Lane songbook, and we did several things. And she was a joy to play for. Also Carrie Smith, I played for Carrie a few times. Abbey Lincoln I played for a long time ago. I remember we did a trio thing with Abbey. We played at a club out in Jersey — Teddy Powell’s. And that was a wonderful experience playing for…
When you, you kind of caught the tail end of the heyday of the big bands I guess, after they kind of had a tough time after World War II. Did you get to do much big band playing because of that?
